sanskrit_verse: दत्तं लेख्ये स्वहस्तं तु ऋणिको यदि निह्नुते । पत्रस्थैः साक्षिभिर् वाचा लेखकस्य मतेन च ॥
transliteration: dattaṃ lekhye svahastaṃ tu ṛṇiko yadi nihnute / patrasthaiḥ sākṣibhir vācā lekhakasya matena ca //
sph_interpretive_translation: When a debtor denies a written document bearing his own hand, the evidence thereof shall be established by the letter itself, by witnesses present at the time of writing, by oral testimony, and by the understanding of the scribe.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is derived from direct personal involvement in the act of documentation
Causation is anchored in conscious assent given at the moment of recordation
Capacity-based responsibility arises from the ability to inscribe or affirm one's intent
Restoration logic requires validation through multiple pramāṇas when denial occurs
Consciousness alignment demands that denial be met with clarity-producing verification
executable_legal_axioms: IF handwriting_unverified AND witness_present THEN collect_oral_testimony = TRUE
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, when a party repudiates a written obligation under their hand, the court shall invoke multi-source pramāṇa verification exclusively for restoring factual alignment, without imputing motive or malice.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality establishes that denial disrupts transactional dharma; anupūrvaśaḥ restores sequence through evidentiary reaffirmation; proportional responsibility lies in re-engagement with truth, not punitive consequence; non-punitive reality rule prevails as denial dissolves upon verification.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Reaffirmation Protocol: Debtor must retrace the act of signing in conscious presence
Witness Reassembly: Summon those present during original documentation
Scribe Consultation: Reconstruct context of writing from recorder’s memory
Document Resonance Alignment: Match handwriting energy signature to debtor's current state
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands executed: denial yields to verification, consciousness is restored, dharma prevails, no punishment arises—only completion.
